summary: Dedicated pool throughput drop: GPU queue starvation and autoscaler thrashing causing request timeouts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer CogniWare reported repeated request timeouts (504s) and elevated p95 latency on their dedicated GPU pool in us-east. The drop started as intermittent spikes on 2026-03-09 and became sustained during business hours on 2026-03-10.

Impact:
- Customer experiencing 20-40% request failures for production inference routes (streaming and standard generate endpoints).
- End-user facing degraded UX for chat and batch scoring.
- Customer is on a committed Dedicated plan; business impact is high.

Observed behavior and quick indicators:
- Request queue lengths on the dedicated pool increased 6-8x during incidents.
- GPU SM utilization observed low (15-30%) while token service latency and PCIe wait metrics spiked.
- Autoscaler logs show repeated scale-up/scale-down cycles roughly every 3-7 minutes for the pool.
- A single tenant in the pool was running many long-running small-batch synchronous requests that appeared to block scheduler fair-share and cause head-of-line queueing.
- External gateway returned 504s; internal serving runtime returned several kernel-timeout and connection-reset logs.

Environment:
- prod cluster: dedicated-pool-cogniware-us-east
- Node type: A100-40GB (mixed 1/2 config)
- Model variants: redwood-alpha-13b (quantized q4), llama-2-70b (fp16)

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Deploy a synthetic workload that mixes high-concurrency short streaming requests with intermittent large-batch scoring jobs to the same dedicated pool.
2) Run sustained bursts (5k reqs/min) for ~20 minutes.
3) Observe queue growth, autoscaler churn, and increases in token latency leading to gateway timeouts.

Relevant logs/metrics (links included below):
- Dedicated pool dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/dedicated/pool/dedicated-pool-cogniware-us-east
- Autoscaler event stream: https://logs.redwood.ai/autoscaler/streams/dedicated-pool-cogniware-us-east
- Recent SRE heap traces and kernel logs attached in internal storage.

Immediate customer impact: high. Customer reported lost queries and has asked for mitigation within SLA window.

2026-03-10 09:10 - Diego Ramos (SRE): Initial hypothesis: autoscaler cooldown too short and prewarm thresholds mis-sized causing thrash + tenant-level head-of-line blocking. Starting live sampling and enabling detailed per-tenant queue metrics.

2026-03-10 11:02 - Diego Ramos: Confirmed autoscaler events: 09:42, 09:49, 09:55, 10:03 — repeated scale-down within minutes of scale-up. Also saw a tenant with a steady stream of 500ms synchronous requests occupying many scheduling slots.

2026-03-11 07:20 - Support: Provisioned isolated fallback pool for CogniWare and started migration trial for high-risk routes. Monitoring impact.
2026-03-12 15:05 - Diego Ramos: Isolation reduced failure rate to <2%. Planning permanent autoscaler policy changes and admission-control fixes. Preparing rollout and changelog.

investigation_notes: Metric correlation shows queue length growth preceded autoscaler actions by ~30-90s, indicating the autoscaler reacts to backlog but cooldown allowed immediate shrinkage before warmup completed.
GPU telemetry: low SM utilization with high page migration/PCIe wait suggests per-request serialization or NVLINK contention on colocated pods rather than GPU compute shortage.
Trace sampling shows scheduler granted many short-lived slots to the noisy tenant; their job mix favors sync requests which block preemption and queue fairness.
Reproduced core symptoms in staging by driving mixed workloads; observed autoscaler cooldown=3m, scale_step=1 node which caused oscillation and repeated GPU warmup overhead.
Checked node dmesg and driver logs — no OOMs or driver crashes. Found intermittent CUDA power-limit throttling messages for one host; flagged for infra to inspect power-capping policy.
SRE ran a controlled test: increasing autoscaler min_nodes to 2 and cooldown to 10m removed thrash and eliminated 504s during synthetic reproduction.

Hypotheses: (1) autoscaler configuration too aggressive for mixed workload; (2) lack of per-tenant admission/fairness; (3) noisy tenant request pattern amplifies warmup costs and causes head-of-line blocking.
Action items created for long-term fixes: autoscaler hysteresis tuning, per-tenant admission controls, prewarm heuristics, and improved telemetry to detect queue-starvation early.
resolution_notes: Temporary measures applied 2026-03-11: moved CogniWare heavy routes to a reserved fallback pool and increased dedicated-pool min_nodes to 2 for 24 hours.
Autoscaler parameters adjusted in prod: cooldown extended to 10m, scale_step increased to 2 for pools with mixed workload labels, warmup prefetch increased to reduce per-node warmup latency.
Implemented short-term scheduler change: per-tenant concurrency cap to reduce head-of-line blocking for synchronous short requests.
Customer confirmed effective reduction in 504s to <2% and p95 latency returned to baseline on 2026-03-12.
Planned long-term: follow-up RFC for autoscaler redesign, per-tenant QoS, and telemetry alerts. Assigned to ENG roadmap Q2.
Post-action: create post-incident review and update runbook with detection query and mitigation steps.
